Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:14:1.hebrew: ואמר ר' ירמיה - האי עבורו מן הטמא דקאמר, היינו שנתעברה מן הקלוט — שפרסותיו קלוטות כגמל, ובן פרה הוא — ואליבא דר' שמעון קרי ליה טמא, ובנו מותר אם דומה לאמו בסימן אחד. אלמא, לאכילה לא בעי ר"ש ראשו ורובו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:14:1.english: And Rabbi Yirmeya says - This [phrase], "its pregnancy from an impure [animal]," that it stated, means that it became pregnant from an animal with closed hooves whose hooves are closed like a camel's, and it is the offspring of a cow; and in accordance with [the view of] Rabbi Shimon, [the baraita] calls it "impure." And its offspring is permitted if it resembles its mother in one characteristic. Evidently, for consumption, Rabbi Shimon does not require its head and the majority of its body.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:16:1.hebrew: זה וזה גורם - ההיתר והאיסור גורמין לזה שיבא — הוא טמא, ואמו טהורה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:16:1.english: [Both] this and that cause [it] - The permitted [factor] and the forbidden [factor] cause this [offspring] to come [into being] — he [the sire] is non-kosher, and its mother is kosher.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:17:1.hebrew: ולד טריפה - ואביו תמים, הרי זה וזה גורם:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:17:1.english: The offspring of a tereifa - And its father is unblemished, [so] behold, [both] this and that cause [it].

Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:18:1.hebrew: דא"כ - דעבורו מן הטמא אסור, לכתוב: "שה כשבים ועזים":
Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:18:1.english: For if so - That its conception from a non-kosher [animal] is forbidden, let [the verse] write: "A sheep of sheep and goats."

Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:23:1.english: Water enters, water exits, and [the fact] that it is turbid is the heat of the flesh - Due to the heat and stench of the flesh.

Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:24:1.hebrew: מטמא - הוי משמע מגופיה דטמא. ״מן הטמא״ משמע מינו של טמא — הן דדמו לחלב:
Rashi on Bekhorot 7a:24:1.english: From a non-kosher [animal] - [This] would imply [something that emerges] from the body of the non-kosher [animal] itself. “From the non-kosher” implies a type of non-kosher [substance] — [namely,] those [fluids] that resemble milk.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 7a:15:1.hebrew: ופליג עליה בחדא - מה שיוכל לדחות דחי כן, משום דבמסקנא לאכילה פשטינן נמי דבעי ר"ש ראשו ורובו:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 7a:15:1.english: "And disagrees with him with regard to one" - Whatever [the Gemara] can deflect, it deflects in this manner, because in the conclusion, we resolve that with regard to consumption as well, Rabbi Shimon requires its head and the majority of its body.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 7a:17:1.hebrew: והא איפכא שמעינן להו ולד טריפה - למ"ד טריפה יולדת, ניחא דפליגי בזה וזה גורם; אלא למ"ד אינה יולדת, מוקמי פלוגתא פרק אלו טריפות (חולין נח.) בעובר ירך אמו, ונתעברה ולבסוף נטרפה. ומיהו אשכחן בעלמא דר' אליעזר סבר זה וזה גורם אסור, ורבנן סברי מותר — גבי שאור חולין ותרומה, ושלהי כל הצלמים (ע"ז מט.) גבי נטל ממנה עצים; אלא לרבי יהושע אייתיה, ואע"ג דלאו דברי הכל הוא. ומה שמזכיר כאן זה וזה גורם, ופר' אותו ואת בנו (חולין עט:) נקט לישנא דחוששין לזרע האב — משום דהכא איירי בדבר הבא מהיתר ואיסור, [שייך שפיר] זה וזה גורם. ומיהו קשה: כיון דאין חוששין לזרע האב, מאיזה טעם תחשב ולד טריפה זה וזה גורם? לא יחשב שאור גורם, וליתסר:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 7a:17:1.english: "But we have heard them [saying] the opposite: The offspring of a tereifa" - According to the one who says that a tereifa can give birth, it is understandable that they disagree over [the principle of] "this and that cause [it]" [zeh vazeh gorem]; but according to the one who says that [a tereifa] cannot give birth, we establish their dispute in chapter "Elu Tereifot" (Chullin 58a) [as being] regarding [whether] a fetus is [considered] the thigh of its mother, and [in a case where] she conceived [while kosher] and was ultimately rendered a tereifa. However, we find elsewhere that Rabbi Eliezer holds [that when] both this and that cause [it], it is forbidden, and the Rabbis hold [it is] permitted — regarding leaven of non-sacred produce [chullin] and of terumah, and at the end of [the chapter entitled] "Kol HaTzelamim" (Avodah Zarah 49a) regarding [one who] took wood from it [an asherah]; rather, [the Gemara] brought it [i.e., the case of the offspring of a tereifa] on account of Rabbi Yehoshua, even though it is not unanimous [that this dispute concerns "this and that cause it"]. And as for [the Gemara] mentioning "this and that cause [it]" here, whereas in chapter "Oto Ve-et Beno" (Chullin 79b) it used the formulation "one is concerned for the seed of the father" — [this is] because here it is dealing with something that comes from [a mixture of] permitted and forbidden [elements], [so the concept of] "this and that cause [it]" is well-suited. However, this is difficult: Since [it is held that] one is not concerned for the seed of the father, for what reason would the offspring of a tereifa be considered [a case where] both this and that cause [it]? Should it not be considered [as if only] the leaven [of prohibition] caused [it] [i.e., as having only a single, forbidden cause], and let it be forbidden?
